scopes.description:
Organization/project/region scope. Accounts with different verified
scopes are never merged, pooled, or silently switched between.

qualification.description: Static implementation scope, not proof this machine/account has been qualified.

ArtifactReadParams.description: Owned in-memory result. No public method accepts a filesystem path.

ConnectionMetadata.description:
Allowlisted adapter output. The service projects this into authorized snapshots.
This record never contains native credential material or private filesystem paths.

amountUsd.description: Null when either token count or a matching price is missing.

basis.description: provider_reported, estimated, or unknown. Never an invoice total.

DecimalString.description: Nonnegative, finite decimal, represented losslessly across all SDKs.

oneOf.description:
A suspended conversation cannot be continued (identity, route, model,
workspace or native history changed or is gone). Never replaced by a
fresh conversation; the host decides whether to start over.

capabilities.description: Runtime-level features such as `turn.input.image` or `session.host_mcp`. Model and adapter support is still per selection.

hydrated.description: True when the summary is built from persisted state that has not yet been reverified.

HostMcpServer.description:
A loopback streamable-HTTP MCP server run by the host application.

`url` must be `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/...` or `http://[::1]:<port>/...`.
The bearer token is a host secret: it is never logged, echoed, or placed on
a command line, and `Debug` redacts it.

allowedTools.description: Tool names (`^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$`) the agent may call on this server.

displayName.description: Host-side label only; validated and never forwarded to a provider.

issuesChanged.description:
True when the affected issues changed. Issue text is available from
`issues.list`, which applies the caller's permission projection.

fingerprint.description: Additional non-secret grouping material. Never a provider token or email.

id.description: Stable across restarts for the same resource and cause.

lastObservation.description: Last known observation while a person decides what to do. Display-only.

IssueEvidence.description: A bounded, sanitized fact supporting an issue. It never contains credentials.

oneOf.description: Still observed or not yet verified as recovered.
The user has seen it; it is still unhealthy.
Notifications are suppressed until this time. The issue is still open.
A later observation verified recovery. Dismissal alone never sets this.

until.description: ISO-8601 time until which notifications are suppressed. Only for `snooze`.

MethodInputs.description: This is the superset of compiled public methods, not a grant or an assertion of live provider support.

NotificationDecision.description:
A deduplicated OS-notification decision. Delivery state is persisted by the
broker so multiple consumers do not each emit the same alert.

NotificationPreferences.description:
Per-install notification preference. Quiet hours use local wall-clock
minutes since midnight and never contain a provider identity.

privateContent.description: Suppress issue text in the OS notification; consumers show it inline.

requiresUserAction.description: True when the runtime cannot safely perform this action on the user's behalf.

ResourceChange.description:
A bounded description of what changed. The full authoritative state remains
`snapshot.get`; consumers that cannot replay must resynchronize.

hostMcpServers.description:
Host-owned loopback MCP servers attached to a native-client session.
In the default read-only mode, only these listed tools may be called.
The separately granted `native_policy` mode also enables the native
client's own tools and policy.

persistent.description:
Keep the native conversation in the client's own history so a
`sessions.suspend` token can resume it after the helper restarts.
Requires the route capability `session.resume.persistent`.

hostMcpServers.description:
Host MCP servers for the resumed session. Tokens never carry the
servers' bearer tokens, so a host re-supplies them here.

resumeToken.description:
Opaque, host-storable token. With `session.resume.persistent` it is
sealed with a per-install key, carries no credentials, and survives
helper restarts; otherwise it lives only as long as the helper.

cursor.description:
Opaque journal cursor at the committed revision. Subscribe with this
value to obtain every inventory change committed after the snapshot.

Timestamp.description: Validated RFC 3339 timestamp, kept as text on the wire.

inputs.description: Staged `inputs.put` references. Each input is consumed by the turn that starts with it.
